items.title: Sixteen Figure 1 settings
paragraphs: The main article and matched SI distinguish two Cu:Sb settings, two mutually exclusive sulfur-source branches, and four temperatures (190, 220, 250 and 280 °C). Figure 1 supplies sixteen condition–phase outcomes; the paper does not establish sixteen independent physical batches.

The general method reports 0.50 mmol Cu(acac)2, 0.50 mmol source-named SbCl3·6H2O and 10 mL OLA, room-temperature degassing for 15 min and nitrogen backfill for 15 min; heat at 170–280 °C under N2. The S/OLA stock is 1.3 mmol S in 1 mL OLA, degassed three times and rapidly injected; the generic 10–30 min stirring span is not assigned as a dwell to every Figure 1 cell. Cool to room temperature; add 15 mL hexane and 15 mL ethanol; centrifuge at 4000 rpm for 5 min; repeat washing three times. Later wash volumes/conditions, yield and drying/storage are not given.

Main Methods uses 1:3 Cu:Sb wording for the high-Cu routes, while Scheme 1, Results and Figure 1 show 3:1. For the Cu3SbS4 subsection, preserve its heading/body product-name mismatch and associated charge wording; do not silently correct either source statement.

items.title: XRD phase assignments and reference structures
paragraphs: XRD discussion assigns CuSbS2 (280 °C/S/OLA) as orthorhombic Pnma, a=6.002, b=3.793, c=14.477 Å; Cu12Sb4S13 (280 °C/S/OLA) as cubic, a=10.333 Å (bulk comparison 10.323 Å); Cu3SbS4 as tetragonal, a=5.378, c=10.729 Å; and Cu3SbS3 (220 °C/thiols) as monoclinic without numerical cell values. Reference structure drawings are literature models, not measured nanocrystal coordinates.
Figure 2 represents these phase/condition contexts but supplies no physical batch identity or cross-technique link.

items.title: TEM/HRTEM morphology
paragraphs: The article explicitly links CuSbS2 morphology to 190 °C using S/OLA: nanoplates, average lateral dimension 325 ± 25 nm and thickness 19 ± 1 nm. The ± statistic is undefined and is not interpreted as a range, SD or SE. No batch ID is supplied; this TEM context is not joined to separate 280 °C XRD lattice parameters.

Other Figure 3 values are phase-level only: Cu12Sb4S13 hollow/irregular-to-cubic forms about 100 ± 30 nm; Cu3SbS4 oblate particles 23 ± 4 nm; Cu3SbS3 near-spherical particles 30 ± 5 nm. Exact route-cell assignments are unresolved. Figure 3 microscopy insets are FFT, not SAED.

items.title: Absorption spectra and experimental Tauc values
paragraphs: Figure 5 is UV–visible absorption and dispersion images, not photoluminescence. Reported positions: CuSbS2 541 nm/2.29 eV and 744 nm/1.66 eV; Cu12Sb4S13 612 nm/2.02 eV and a 470 nm/2.64 eV shoulder; Cu3SbS4 410 nm/3.02 eV, 547 nm/2.26 eV and 677 nm/1.83 eV shoulders; Cu3SbS3 642 nm/1.93 eV.
Experimental Tauc values: CuSbS2 indirect 1.1 eV; Cu3SbS3 direct 1.4 eV; Cu3SbS4 indirect 1.2 eV; Cu12Sb4S13 direct 1.6 eV. These are phase-level contexts, not exact map-cell sample links.

items.title: Calculated electronic structure and optical response
paragraphs: VASP/PAW/PBE/HSE06 calculations are modeled results, distinct from measurements. HSE06 values: CuSbS2 indirect 1.6 eV (PBE about 0.85 eV), Cu3SbS3 direct 1.5 eV, Cu3SbS4 indirect 2.5 eV. The stoichiometric 58-atom Cu12Sb4S13 model is metallic at EF; Figure 7’s 1.7 eV label is above EF. The discussion of electron addition/off-stoichiometry uses a rigid shift, not supplied off-stoichiometric coordinates.

Figure 8 is calculated optical absorption/dielectric response, separate from measured Figure 5. The proposed quasi-2D charge localization for Cu3SbS4 is an author interpretation. Device performance is absent; the article says device work is ongoing.
